---
title: "Notation"
subtitle: "One set of symbols for the whole week"
---

When a paper uses a symbol that clashes with ours, we keep its letter with a method subscript
and note the paper's original symbol here.

| Symbol | Meaning | Paper symbol it replaces |
|---|---|---|
| $s, a, s'$ | state, action, next state | |
| $\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}$ | state and action sets | |
| $r_t$ | reward received after action $a_t$ (Sutton and Barto write $R_{t+1}$) | |
| $r(s,a)$ | expected reward; the array `R[s, a]` holds it | |
| $P(s' \mid s,a)$ | transition probability; the array `P[s, a, s']` | |
| $\gamma$ | discount factor (only this) | Ouyang et al.'s pretraining coefficient → $c_{\text{ptx}}$ |
| $G_t$ | return from time $t$ | |
| $\pi$, $\pi(a \mid s)$ | target policy | |
| $\pi_b$ | behavior policy (frees $b$ for the baseline $b(s)$) | Dudík et al.'s $p$; CQL's $\pi_\beta$ |
| $\pi_{\text{ref}}$ | reference policy (language models) | |
| $V^\pi, Q^\pi, A^\pi$ | state value, action value, advantage | |
| $V$, $Q$ | learned estimates of $V^\pi$ (or $V^*$) and of $Q^\pi$ (or $Q^*$); the arrays `V[s]` and `Q[s, a]` (Sutton and Barto's $V$, $Q$ against their $v_\pi$, $q_\pi$) | |
| $N(s)$ | number of first visits to $s$ averaged by Monte Carlo (Module 3) | |
| $Q_0$, $v_0$ | the starting value of every entry of $Q$ or $V$ (`q0`, `v0` in code); Module 3's optimistic start is $Q_0 = 10$ | |
| $T$ | the number of transitions in an episode: states $s_0, \dots, s_T$, rewards $r_0, \dots, r_{T-1}$; in Module 4, the number of rounds of a bandit run (rounds $t = 0, \dots, T-1$) | Lattimore and Szepesvári's horizon $n$ |
| $G_t^{(n)}$ | the $n$-step return: $n$ sampled rewards, then $\gamma^n V(s_{t+n})$ (Module 3) | Sutton and Barto's $G_{t:t+n}$ |
| `terminated`, `truncated` | Gymnasium's two episode ends: a terminal state (no bootstrap) and a cut (bootstrap) | |
| online return | the sum of an episode's rewards while learning, undiscounted (Module 3's cliff contrast) | Sutton and Barto's "sum of rewards during episode" |
| $\lVert x \rVert_\infty$ | the max norm, $\max_s \lvert x(s) \rvert$: the largest entry in absolute value | |
| $\eta$ | an accuracy or an error bound: the error $\lVert V_k - V^\pi \rVert_\infty$ you want to reach (Module 1), a bound $\lVert Q - Q^* \rVert_\infty \le \eta$ (Module 2), or the deviation of a sample mean in Hoeffding's inequality (Module 4); not $\varepsilon$, the exploration rate | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\varepsilon$ in their Eq. 5.8 |
| $\mathrm{tol}$ | stopping threshold on the change per sweep, $\lVert V_{k+1} - V_k \rVert_\infty$ | |
| $\hat{A}_t$ | advantage estimate | |
| $\delta_t$ | TD error | Hoeffding's failure probability → $p_{\text{fail}}$ |
| $\alpha$ | step size (only this) | SAC's temperature → $\alpha_{\text{ent}}$; CQL's weight → $\alpha_{\text{cql}}$ |
| $\varepsilon$ | exploration rate ($\varepsilon$-greedy) | |
| $\varepsilon_{\text{clip}}$ | PPO clipping range | PPO's $\epsilon$ |
| $\lambda$ | λ-return and GAE (the same object) | ridge regularizer → $\lambda_{\text{ridge}}$ |
| $\rho_t$, $\rho_{0:t}$ | importance ratio $\pi/\pi_b$ and its running product; in PPO $\rho_t(\theta) = \pi_\theta/\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}$ | PPO's $r_t(\theta)$ |
| $\beta$ | KL coefficient (RLHF, DPO); AWR weights are written $\exp(\hat{A}/\beta)$ | IQL's inverse temperature |
| $c$ | exploration-bonus coefficient | LinUCB's $\alpha$; MBIE-EB's $\beta$ |
| $c_V, c_H$ | PPO value-loss and entropy weights | PPO's $c_1, c_2$ |
| $K$ | GRPO group size | DeepSeekMath's $G$ (clashes with $G_t$) |
| $N(s,a)$ | visit count ($n$ stays the n-step length); in Module 2 also $N$, the number of samples drawn at every $(s,a)$ | MBIE-EB's $n(s,a)$ |
| $\Lambda_a$ | LinUCB Gram matrix | Li et al.'s $A_a$ |
| $r(a)$, $r^*$ | a bandit's mean reward of arm $a$ (a bandit has one state, so $r(s, a)$ becomes $r(a)$), and the best mean, $r^* = \max_a r(a)$ (Module 4) | Auer et al.'s and Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\mu_a$, $\mu^*$ ($\mu$ is our state weighting) |
| $\Delta_a$ | the gap of arm $a$, $r^* - r(a)$ | |
| $N_t(a)$, $\hat r_t(a)$ | the number of pulls of arm $a$ in rounds $0, \dots, t-1$, and the mean of their rewards (Module 4; `counts[a]` and `sums[a] / counts[a]` in code) | Auer et al.'s $n_j$, $T_j(n)$, $\bar x_j$; Lattimore and Szepesvári's $T_i(t)$, $\hat\mu_i(t)$ |
| $\mathrm{Reg}_T$ | pseudo-regret after $T$ rounds, $\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \big(r^* - r(a_t)\big) = \sum_a \Delta_a N_T(a)$; its expectation is the regret | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\bar R_n$ (pseudo-regret) and $R_n$ (regret) |
| $p_{\text{fail}}$ | the failure probability of a confidence bound (Hoeffding's inequality) | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\delta$ |
| $U_t(a)$ | UCB1's index: $\hat r_t(a) + \sqrt{2 \ln t / N_t(a)}$, infinite for an arm never pulled | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\mathrm{UCB}_i$ |
| $B$ | the width of the reward range: rewards in $[0, B]$ (Module 4; UCB1 assumes $B = 1$) | |
| $S_t(a)$, $F_t(a)$ | the rewards of 1 and of 0 among arm $a$'s pulls (Bernoulli rewards), so the posterior from a uniform prior is $\mathrm{Beta}(1 + S_t(a), 1 + F_t(a))$ (Module 4) | Russo et al.'s $\alpha_k - 1$, $\beta_k - 1$ ($\alpha$ and $\beta$ are our step size and KL coefficient) |
| $\tilde r_t(a)$ | a mean for arm $a$ drawn from its posterior in Thompson sampling (Module 4) | Russo et al.'s $\hat\theta_k$ ($\theta$ is our policy parameters) |
| $\theta$, $w$, $\phi(s)$ | policy parameters, value parameters, features | |
| $\mu$, $d$ | state weighting, feature dimension | |
| $\tau$, $\tau_e$ | trajectory, IQL expectile | |
| $V^*, Q^*, \pi^*$ | optimal state value, action value and policy; $V^*(s) = \max_a Q^*(s, a)$ | |
| $T^\pi, T^*$ | the Bellman expectation operator $T^\pi V = r_\pi + \gamma P_\pi V$ and the optimality operator $(T^* V)(s) = \max_a [r(s,a) + \gamma \sum_{s'} P(s' \mid s,a) V(s')]$ | |
| $\pi_Q$ | the greedy policy of an action-value array $Q$: $\pi_Q(s) = \arg\max_a Q(s, a)$ | |
| $\hat P, \hat r$ | transition and reward estimates from counts (Module 2); the arrays `P_hat[s, a, s']` and `R_hat[s, a]`; $\hat V^\pi, \hat\pi$ are values and the plan in the estimated model | |
| $\lVert p - q \rVert_1$ | the $\ell_1$ distance between two distributions, $\sum_{s'} \lvert p(s') - q(s') \rvert$, between 0 and 2 | |
| $\varepsilon_P$ | model error, $\max_{s,a} \lVert P(\cdot \mid s,a) - \hat P(\cdot \mid s,a) \rVert_1$ (Module 2) | |
| $\varepsilon_R$ | reward error, $\max_{s,a} \lvert r(s,a) - \hat r(s,a) \rvert$ (Module 2) | |
| $Z(x)$ | partition function in the KL-regularized optimum | |
| $H$ | horizon | |
| $x$, $x_t$ | a context: what the agent observes about the user in round $t$ (Module 5); in RecSim $x \in \mathbb{R}^5$ | Li et al.'s $x_{t,a}$; Agrawal and Goyal's $b_i(t)$ |
| $\phi(x)$ | Module 5's features of a context, $\phi(x) = (x, 1)$, with $d = 6$ entries | |
| $K$ | the number of arms (items) of a bandit, Module 4's $\lvert \mathcal{A} \rvert$ (Modules 5 and 13); items are numbered 0 to $K - 1$ | |
| $r(x, a)$ | the mean reward of item $a$ in context $x$; in RecSim, the click probability (Module 5). Module 5's pseudo-regret is Module 4's $\mathrm{Reg}_T$, measured against the best item for each context | RecSim's docstring writes $\mu(x, a)$ ($\mu$ is our state weighting) |
| $\theta_a$, $\theta^{\text{alt}}_a$ | Module 5: item $a$'s hidden RecSim parameters, `env.theta` and `env.theta_alt` (the simulator's, not a learner's) | |
| $w^*_a$, $\hat w_a$, $\tilde w_a$ | Module 5: item $a$'s true linear reward parameter $(0.15\,\theta_a, 0.5)$, its ridge estimate $\Lambda_a^{-1} b_a$ (code: `w_hat`), and a Thompson draw | Li et al.'s $\theta_a$; Agrawal and Goyal's $\mu$, $\hat\mu(t)$, $\tilde\mu(t)$ |
| $b_a$ | Module 5: item $a$'s sum $\sum_i r_i\, \phi_i$; $\hat w_a = \Lambda_a^{-1} b_a$ (code: `A` is $\Lambda_a$, `A_inv`, `b`) | Li et al.'s $b_a$ |
| $\lVert \phi \rVert_{\Lambda^{-1}}$ | the width $\sqrt{\phi^\top \Lambda^{-1} \phi}$ of a prediction in direction $\phi$ (Module 5); $\lVert v \rVert_\Lambda = \sqrt{v^\top \Lambda v}$ | |
| $\kappa$, $\kappa_t$ | the radius of LinUCB's confidence ellipsoid $\lVert w - \hat w \rVert_\Lambda \le \kappa$ (Module 5); $\kappa_t$ is the radius in round $t$, and $\zeta_t$ the logarithmic term inside it, in Module 5's collapsed Theorem 20.5 | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\sqrt{\beta_t}$ (our $\beta$ is the KL coefficient) |
| $v$ | linear Thompson sampling's scale, $\tilde w_a \sim \mathcal{N}(\hat w_a, v^2 \Lambda_a^{-1})$ (Module 5); not $v_0$ | Agrawal and Goyal's $v$; MABWiser's `alpha` for LinTS |
| $\xi_i$ | the noise of one observation, $r_i - w^{*\top}\phi_i$ (Module 5) | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $\eta_t$ (our $\eta$ is an error bound) |
| $\sigma$ | the scale of sub-Gaussian noise (Module 5) | Agrawal and Goyal's $R$ |
| $M$ | a bound on $\lVert w^* \rVert_2$ (Module 5, collapsed) | Lattimore and Szepesvári's $m_2$ |
| $\nu$, $\omega$ | RecSim's misspecification weight and drift rate (Module 5) | RecSim's `misspec` and `drift` |
| $p_i$ | the propensity of logged row $i$, $\pi_b(a_i \mid x_i)$ (Module 5); the array `log.P` | |
| $a_{\text{UCB}}(x)$ | the item with the highest LinUCB score for context $x$ (Module 5) | |
| $P_\pi$, $r_\pi$ | the state-to-state transition matrix and the expected reward under a fixed policy $\pi$, $P_\pi(s, s') = \sum_a \pi(a \mid s) P(s' \mid s, a)$ (Module 1; Module 6 calls $P_\pi$ the policy chain) | |
| $h(s)$ | hitting time: the expected number of steps to first reach a target state from $s$ (Module 6) | |
| $u_s$ | crossing time: the expected number of steps to first reach $s + 1$ from $s$ in a chain (Module 6) | |
| $p_\rightarrow$, $p_\leftarrow$ | the per-step probabilities of moving right and left in a chain under a fixed policy (Module 6) | |
| $r_{\max}$, $V_{\max}$ | the largest reward, and $V_{\max} = r_{\max}/(1 - \gamma)$, the largest discounted return when every reward lies in $[0, r_{\max}]$ (Module 6's optimistic start) | |
| $\tilde Q, \tilde V$ | MBIE-EB's optimistic action values and state values: the solution of the estimated model's backup with the bonus $c/\sqrt{N(s,a)}$ in the reward (Module 6) | Strehl and Littman's $\tilde Q$ (same) |
| $m$ | MBIE's model-size limit: how many visits of a pair the model uses (Module 6, reference only) | |
| $\nu(s)$ | visitation: the fraction of a run's steps spent in state $s$ (Module 6) | |
| $\bar r^*_t$ | the optimal policy's expected reward at step $t$ from the start (Module 6). Module 6 uses Module 4's $\mathrm{Reg}_T$ for $\sum_{t=0}^{T-1} \big(\bar r^*_t - r(s_t, a_t)\big)$, cumulative regret against the DP optimum | |
| $\hat N(x)$ | pseudo-count of a state $x$, derived from a density model (Module 6, section 6) | Bellemare et al.'s $\hat N_n(x)$ |
| $\rho_{\text{dens}}, \rho'_{\text{dens}}$ | a density model's probability of a state before and after seeing it once more (Module 6, reference only) | Bellemare et al.'s $\rho_n, \rho'_n$ (clash with $\rho_t$) |
| $f, \hat f$ | RND's fixed random target network and its trained predictor (Module 6, section 6) | |
| $Q(s, a; w)$, $w^-$ | Module 8: the online network and the parameters of the target network, a copy of $w$ refreshed every `target_sync` steps | Mnih et al.'s $\theta$, $\theta^-$ and van Hasselt et al.'s $\theta_t$, $\theta^-_t$ ($\theta$ is our policy parameters) |
| $\mathcal{D}$, $\mathcal{B}$, $\lvert \mathcal{B} \rvert$ | Module 8: the replay buffer, a minibatch drawn from it, and the batch size | Mnih et al.'s $D$ (our $D$ is Module 7's $\operatorname{diag}(\mu)$) |
| $\mathrm{term}_i$, $\mathrm{trunc}_i$ | Module 8: 1 if transition $i$ ended at a terminal state (Gymnasium's `terminated`), or was cut (`truncated`); 0 otherwise | |
| $y_i$ | Module 8: the TD target of transition $i$ of a minibatch | Mnih et al.'s $y_j$; van Hasselt et al.'s $Y_t$ |
| $\operatorname{huber}_\psi$, $\psi$ | Module 8: the Huber loss with threshold $\psi$, $\tfrac12 x^2$ for $\lvert x \rvert \le \psi$ and $\psi(\lvert x \rvert - \tfrac12 \psi)$ beyond; its derivative is $\operatorname{clip}(x, -\psi, \psi)$ (`threshold` in code) | PyTorch's `delta` in `huber_loss` ($\delta$ is our TD error) |
| $k$ | Module 8: the number of target copies that follow a gradient step, in "(sync lag)", $(1 - \gamma^k)/(1 - \gamma)$ | |
| $C$ | Module 8: the mean squared estimation error in van Hasselt et al.'s Theorem 1 | van Hasselt et al.'s $C$ (same); Mnih et al.'s $C$ is the copy interval, our `target_sync` |
| $\hat Q(a)$, $a^\star_i$ | Module 8: random estimates of one state's action values (the max bias), and Double DQN's next action $\arg\max_{a'} Q(s'_i, a'; w)$ | |
| $\alpha_{\text{per}}$, $\beta_{\text{per}}$ | Module 8, reference only: prioritized replay's prioritization and importance-weight exponents | Schaul et al.'s $\alpha$, $\beta$ |
| $\bar Q_t$, $\bar G_t$ | at log step $t$: the mean over a fixed set of start states of $\max_a Q(s, a; w_t)$, and the mean discounted return $G_0$ of the episodes that ended in the 5,000 steps before $t$; $\bar Q_t - \bar G_t$ is the Q drift (Module 9; `q_drift` in code) | |
| relative TD error | the mean $\lvert\delta\rvert$ over a log interval's batches divided by the mean over their rows of $\max_a Q(s, a; w)$ (Module 9; `td_error_scale` in code); no symbol | |
| $z_1, \dots, z_n$; $z_{(i)}$ | one result per seed, and the $i$-th smallest of them (Module 9) | Agarwal et al.'s $x_{1:M,1:N}$ for $N$ runs on $M$ tasks (our $x$ is a context) |
| $\ell$ | the number of values the IQM drops from each end, $\ell = \lfloor n/4 \rfloor$ (Module 9) | |
| $\operatorname{IQM}(z)$ | the interquartile mean, $\frac{1}{n - 2\ell}\sum_{i=\ell+1}^{n-\ell} z_{(i)}$: SciPy's `trim_mean(z, 0.25)` (Module 9) | |
| $z^{(b)}$, $n_{\text{boot}}$ | the $b$-th bootstrap resample ($n$ draws from $z$ with replacement) and the number of resamples (Module 9; `n_boot = 5000` in `prl.evaluate`) | |
| $\hat Z_i$ | a noisy estimate of configuration $i$'s score, as in a sweep (Module 9, section 6) | |
